newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Former U.S. president says Nigeria postpones polls.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. president says Nigeria postpones polls.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter said on Monday Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha told him state elections set for the second half of 1997 would instead be held next year.

"During our discussion, General Abacha told me that progress is being made in the implementation of the transition to a civilian democratic government, and that elections of governors will no longer be this year but next year," Carter told reporters.

Nigeria's government has been widely expected to shift the election of legislators and governors for the states after the five registered political parties suggested the state polls be held together with the presidential election in 1998.
Government opponents, however, say a postponment will be further evidence that Abacha is not serious about handing over to an elected president on October 1, 1998, as he has promised.

Carter said Abacha had assured him the government "is committed to free and fair elections during the transition period, and that a democratically elected government will surely be in place in October 1998 as promised."

The former American leader said he had raised with Abacha the issue of political detainees -- among them former head of state General Obasanjo and his then deputy General Shehu Musa Yar'Adua and Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of an annulled 1993 presidential election.
"I did not receive any encouraging response in the appeal for their release," Carter said.
Obasanjo and Yar'Adua were in power in the 1970s when Carter visited Nigeria as president. The two men were among those jailed in 1995 for an alleged plot to topple Abacha.
Relations between Nigeria and Western states are strained over lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
